chunks: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a mosque that is in a house, whose residents wish to expand with a part of it or move it from its place, he said: “There is no harm in that.”

He said: So I said, would a place that had been a latrine for a time be suitable to be cleaned and made into a mosque? He said: “Yes, if enough soil is cast over it to cover it, for that cleanses it and purifies it.”

key_terms.حُشًّا: a latrine or place used for relieving oneself
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression indicating permissibility
key_terms.مَسْجِدٍ: a mosque or designated place of sajdah and worship
key_terms.ٱلتُّرَابِ: soil or earth placed over the area
key_terms.ٱلدَّارِ: the house or dwelling in which the mosque space is located

ai.seo_question: Can a mosque inside a house be moved or expanded, and can a former latrine area be turned into a mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning mosques within private homes and the purification of land for mosque use. It permits altering or relocating such a mosque space and affirms that a place formerly used as a latrine may be made into a mosque if it is covered with soil in a manner that cleanses and purifies it.
